Subject: Renewal paperwork + capacity uplift — draft for legal

Hi Amy,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached are our proposed updates to the MSA and the order form reflecting Acme's 2.5x capacity uplift and a 24-month term. High-level changes:
- Term: 24 months, effective 2028-02-01.
- Capacity: 2.5x uplift on committed units, exhibit E updated to reflect consumption tiers.
- SLA: minor tweaks to credits schedule; we flagged a proposed cap.
- Data retention: default 90 days for caching artifacts; customer-requested logs to be preserved per Exhibit C.

Can your legal team send back redlines and call out any must-haves by end of day Tuesday (2028-01-10)? We want to fold any material asks into the counters before sending to procurement.

Attachments: Redline_MSA_ACME_v1.docx, ACME_Renewal_OrderForm_v1.xlsx

Best,
Kimberly Park

Subject: Re: Renewal paperwork + capacity uplift — draft for legal

Kimberly —

Thanks for sending this over. Attached are Acme Legal's redlines (see comments inline). Key open items we flagged:
1) SLA credits: Acme prefers uncapped credits for availability below 99.5% (we called this out in Sec 7.2).
2) Data retention & customer data handling: need clarity on backup retention in Exhibit C — can you confirm retention window for logs vs. usage KV cache?
3) Order form: we noted a discrepancy in the billing cadence for burst capacity (Exhibit E).

Happy to hop on a 30-minute sync if that helps. We generally need final paper by 2028-01-12 for our Q1 procurement cycle.

Attachment: Redline_MSA_ACME_v1_comments.docx

—Amy Walsh
VP, Legal Operations
Acme Corp
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-01-06T08:04:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal paperwork + capacity uplift — incoming redlines from Acme

Folks — forwarding Amy's redlines (see quoted message below). Quick thoughts and proposed actions:

- SLA credits: they want uncapped credits for sustained low availability. That's a hard no for us on production SLAs; propose we counter with a 10% annual credit cap and a faster remediation commitment (24-hour incident response + escalation path).
- Data retention: their ask conflates KV cache retention and persisted logs. Recommend we keep KV cache at 90 days and offer a paid-retention option for logs beyond 90 days.
- Burst billing mismatch: Ops should confirm billing cadence; ask Finance to model revenue impact of changing cadence.

Action items (internal):
1) Marissa: confirm whether a 10% cap on SLA credits is acceptable from a commercial perspective.
2) Karthik: loop in Observability/Infra to confirm technical feasibility of separating KV cache vs persisted logs and estimate cost.
3) I'll draft a redline response and a short comment table for their legal team; target send by EOD 2028-01-07.

Attachment: internal-action-items.pdf

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal paperwork + capacity uplift — incoming redlines from Acme

Kim — quick read: the 10% cap on SLA credits feels reasonable for a renewal of this scale. If we absorb that cap we should tighten the remediation SLA and preserve our right to rollback burst capacity abuse. On the data side, offering an add-on retention option is standard and should be fine — Ops will need to price it.

Approve moving forward with the counterproposal:
- Offer: 10% annual cap on credits; accelerated incident response (24h) + named escalation contact.
- Data: KV cache default 90d; paid retention add-on for logs/backups.

Once Karthik confirms feasibility, Kimberly, send the counter redline to Amy and copy Procurement.

—Marissa
Sr. Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Amy —

Thanks for the detailed review. Attached is a clean counter with our edits incorporated (see summary below):
- SLA credits: counter with a 10% annual cap and a guaranteed 24-hour incident response and named escalation. (See Sec 7.2)
- Data retention: default KV cache 90 days; logs/backups available as a paid retention add-on. (Exhibit C)
- Burst billing cadence: clarified to align with monthly billing in Exhibit E.

If that looks acceptable, we can move straight to DocuSign. We will also provide a short summary table of changes for Procurement.

Attachments: Redline_MSA_ACME_v2.docx
